briefs.headline: Tottenham beat Chelsea 2-0 at Stamford Bridge as Palmer is sent off
briefs.summary: Tottenham won at Chelsea for only the second time in 34 Premier League visits on Saturday, 2-0 in rain and wind at Stamford Bridge. Mike Penders, on his first league start for the injured Emiliano Martinez, punched Mateus Fernandes' 77th-minute corner into his own net; Cole Palmer was sent off in the 80th for a second yellow, a late tackle on Conor Gallagher; and Mathys Tel ran from his own half past Maxence Lacroix and scored from 20 yards in the 87th. Tottenham had 68.5 percent of the ball and 15 shots to seven. Chelsea were without Joao Pedro, hurt in training Friday; Tottenham lost James Maddison to an injury early in the second half. Xabi Alonso said "we win and we lose together"; Roberto De Zerbi called his side "a complete team." Chelsea stay 4th on 13 points and host Manchester United on Saturday at 8:30 a.m. ET; Tottenham rise to 12th on 9 and host Crystal Palace on Saturday at 1:30 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Iraola rules Szoboszlai out against Brighton and tells Ngumoha to ignore the noise
briefs.summary: Andoni Iraola said at his Friday news conference that Dominik Szoboszlai, who has not trained with the group since going off against Brentford, will miss Sunday's match against Brighton at Anfield, that Victor Munoz is doubtful with a knock from the same match, and that Bradley Barcola trained normally after missing Thursday's session. Asked about Rio Ngumoha, the 18-year-old whose two-goal night against Villarreal on Tuesday he called one of his best, Iraola said "the outside noise, when it's good, when it's bad, it affects, but we have to not be affected by those things." Liverpool, 5th on 12 points, kick off at 10 a.m. ET (2 p.m. GMT, British clocks having gone back overnight) against a Brighton side 3rd on 16.

briefs.headline: Jackson, limping after practice, says playing against the Bengals is a pain-tolerance call
briefs.summary: Lamar Jackson is officially questionable for Sunday's 1 p.m. ET game against Cincinnati in Baltimore and said after Friday's practice, to which he walked with a limp, that he has a high ankle sprain and that "right now, I'm heading in the right direction. I can't call it right now." He practiced on a limited basis all week for the first time since the Oct. 4 injury and said the swelling is down but planting his left foot still hurts; coach Jesse Minter said the Ravens will take as long as they need before naming a starter, which points to a game-time decision. Tyler Huntley would start a third straight game if Jackson sits. Since 2018 Baltimore has beaten the Bengals 11 times in 13 games with Jackson and lost all three without him.

briefs.headline: Todd Benzinger, who caught the last out of the Reds' 1990 World Series, dies at 63
briefs.summary: The Reds announced Thursday that Todd Benzinger, their first baseman from 1989 to 1991 and the man who squeezed the final out of the 1990 World Series sweep of Oakland, died Wednesday at 63. Benzinger played nine major league seasons, debuting with Boston in 1987 and finishing with San Francisco in 1995, managed Class A Dayton in 2009 and 2010, and remained active in youth baseball in New Richmond, Ohio, where he went to high school. Rick Walls, executive director of the Reds Hall of Fame and Museum, said Benzinger "remained close to the Cincinnati community" and was a regular at the Reds Caravan, fantasy camp and Redsfest. No cause was given.

briefs.headline: Browns expect Judkins back and Sampson activated for Sunday's game at Tennessee
briefs.summary: Quinshon Judkins, Cleveland's leading rusher with 230 yards, was left off Friday's injury report after missing last week's game with an ankle injury, and coach Todd Monken said he anticipates Dylan Sampson, who opened the season as Judkins' backup, will be activated from injured reserve after missing five games with a knee injury suffered on a kickoff return in the opener. Both are expected to play when the Browns, winners of four of their first six, visit the Titans at 1 p.m. ET on CBS; Tennessee has won once.

briefs.headline: Crew beat Toronto 4-2 behind two Amundsen goals and three Chambost assists
briefs.summary: Columbus scored four times in the first hour at ScottsMiracle-Gro Field on Saturday and held on with 10 men for a third straight win and a fifth in six. Gonzalo Tapia tapped in Mohamed Farsi's cross in the 16th minute, Malte Amundsen headed in a Dylan Chambost corner in the 21st and turned in another Chambost ball in the 48th for his first multi-goal MLS game, and Brooks Lennon added the fourth in the 59th, also from Chambost. Daniel Salloi headed one back in the 69th, Sekou Bangoura was sent off for a second yellow a minute later and Josh Sargent scored from distance in the 81st; Patrick Schulte made five saves before 19,487. The Crew (11 wins, 5 draws, 15 losses) are 10th in the East on 38 points, one behind 9th-place Red Bull New York, with three matches left, starting Wednesday at FC Dallas at 8:30 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: FC Cincinnati beat D.C. United 2-0 on Evander's strike for a second win in four days
briefs.summary: Evander scored from well outside the box in the 35th minute at Audi Field on Saturday night and set up Tom Barlow's finish from the center of the box in the 52nd as Cincinnati followed Wednesday's home win over the same opponent with a 2-0 victory in Washington before 16,046. Roman Celentano's two saves gave Cincinnati a third clean sheet of the season and its first since April 25; D.C. United had 57 percent of possession and 13 shots but put two on target and have lost three straight. Cincinnati (11 wins, 9 draws, 11 losses) move to 42 points, level with 7th-place Orlando and listed 8th in the East on the ESPN table, three clear of 9th-place Red Bull New York, with three matches left, beginning Wednesday at Inter Miami at 7:30 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Ohio beats Eastern Michigan 24-20 on a 100-yard kickoff return and a goal-line stand
briefs.summary: Darren James-Hamilton returned the kickoff 100 yards for a touchdown 13 seconds after Eastern Michigan had gone 98 yards to take the lead with 3:53 left, and Ohio's defense then stopped the Eagles four times from inside the 5-yard line in the final half-minute, the last a fourth-down incompletion from the 16 after an intentional-grounding penalty on a Michael Molnar sack, to win at Peden Stadium on Saturday before 18,813. Nick Poulos completed 19 of 29 passes for 266 yards, including a 78-yard catch-and-run score by Dom Dorwart, and ran for a 1-yard touchdown; Molnar made 18 tackles. The Bobcats, six wins and two losses and unbeaten in four MAC games, have won 17 straight at home, the longest streak in the nation, and are idle until Nov. 3 at Akron, 7 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Spurs lose to Houston on a last-second block, then beat Dallas for a first win
briefs.summary: San Antonio lost 114 to 110 to the Rockets in Austin on Friday night when Amen Thompson blocked Victor Wembanyama's tying layup with under a second left and Fred VanVleet made two free throws; Alperen Sengun scored 29 and Wembanyama had 25 points and 13 rebounds, though a banked three-pointer on the previous possession was waved off because Mitch Johnson had called timeout. On Saturday in Dallas the Spurs won 122 to 106 for their first victory of the season, opening the fourth quarter with 17 points to five against a Mavericks side missing Cooper Flagg (shoulder) and Kyrie Irving (rest); Wembanyama had 23 points and four blocks, Dylan Harper 22, and De'Aaron Fox and Stephon Castle 19 apiece. San Antonio, one win and two losses, hosts Sacramento on Tuesday at 8 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Concacaf moves the USMNT's Nations League first leg against Haiti to Miami
briefs.summary: Concacaf approved the Haitian federation's request Thursday to move its home leg of the Nations League quarterfinal against the United States from Kingston, Jamaica, to Nu Stadium in Miami on Nov. 14, so both legs will be played on U.S. soil, with the return in Cincinnati on Nov. 17. Haiti has not played at home since 2021 and its national stadium was taken over by gangs in 2024; Concacaf said the arrangement, which lets Haiti play designated home matches in the opponent's territory, stands for as long as the security situation persists and needs approval match by match. U.S. Soccer also confirmed Tuesday that the team will close 2026 with a friendly against Jamaica in Fort Lauderdale on Dec. 13 at 3:30 p.m. ET, a December camp replacing the usual January one.

briefs.headline: West Virginia beats TCU 24-20 as Hawkins scores three times and a late fumble holds
briefs.summary: Michael Hawkins Jr. ran for touchdowns of 2 and 36 yards and threw a 13-yard scoring pass to Cam Cook with 11:28 left, and West Virginia's defense ended TCU's final drive when David Afogho hit Jaden Craig as he dropped back and Ben Cutter recovered the fumble at the Mountaineers' 14 with 34 seconds to go, on Saturday in Fort Worth before 36,216. Craig completed his first 12 passes and finished 33 of 47 for 372 yards, and TCU outgained West Virginia 484 yards to 265 and held the ball more than 37 minutes but fumbled four times and lost three. The Mountaineers, five wins and three losses, have passed last season's win total; Rich Rodriguez said "any win's a big win, and a win on the road is especially big." West Virginia is idle Saturday and plays next at Texas Tech on Nov. 7.

Tottenham are 12th in the Premier League on 9 points from 8 matches (2-3-3, GD -2), up from 16th after Saturday's win at Chelsea, level on points with 11th-place Hull (9 from 7) and one above 13th-place Fulham, per the ESPN eng.1 standings page read at 5:46 a.m. ET Sunday.

Columbus are 10th in the MLS Eastern Conference on 38 points from 31 matches (11-5-15, GD +1), up from 11th after Saturday's win, one point below 9th-place Red Bull New York (39) and four below 8th-place FC Cincinnati (42), per the ESPN usa.1 standings page read at 5:46 a.m. ET Sunday; three matches remain, Wednesday at Dallas, Oct. 31 against D.C. The Browns are 4-2 (W1), listed 1st in the AFC North in a three-way tie at 4-2 with Pittsburgh and Baltimore and 4th in the AFC, 1.5 games behind the 5-0 Chiefs, per the ESPN NFL standings page read at 5:46 a.m. ET Sunday, unchanged before today's 1 p.m. ET game at Tennessee.

The Bengals are 3-2 (W1), 4th in the AFC North, half a game behind the three 4-2 teams above them and 8th in the AFC, per the ESPN NFL standings page read at 5:46 a.m. ET Sunday, unchanged before today's 1 p.m. ET game at Baltimore.

West Virginia is 5-3 overall (W2) after Saturday's win at TCU, listed 8th of 16 on the ESPN Big 12 standings page read at 5:46 a.m. ET Sunday, up from 10th; Utah leads at 7-0, and TCU is 3-4 and listed 15th. The Mountaineers are idle Saturday and play next Nov. 7 at Texas Tech.

The Spurs are 1-2 (W1) and two games behind 3-0 Houston in the Southwest Division, where Memphis is 2-0 and half a game back and Dallas is also 1-2, and ESPN's seed column lists San Antonio 11th of 15 in the West, per the ESPN NBA standings page read at 5:46 a.m. ET Sunday; the Spurs host Sacramento on Tuesday and Minnesota on Saturday and play at Utah on Wednesday.

briefs.headline: Brewers rally from 4-0 down to beat the Rays 5-4 and lead the World Series 2-0
briefs.summary: Sal Frelick tied Game 2 with a sixth-inning homer to center, his first since July 11, and Cooper Pratt's seventh-inning single off the bullpen put Milwaukee ahead Saturday night after Tampa Bay scored four in the first against rookie Logan Henderson, Liam Hicks hitting a two-run homer. Abner Uribe got the win with 1 1/3 hitless innings and Aaron Ashby struck out Yandy Diaz with Jonny DeLuca on third to end it. Milwaukee has won seven straight in the postseason and is the fifth team to overcome two four-run deficits in one October; the Rays made two errors and dropped a flyball. In Game 1 on Friday, Trevor Megill struck out DeLuca with the bases loaded after a replay overturned a game-ending double play, and Christian Yelich's first-inning RBI triple stood up in a 3-2 win. Game 3 is Monday night at Tropicana Field in St. Petersburg; 46 of the 57 previous teams up 2-0 in the Series won it.

briefs.headline: UCF beats No. 2 BYU 39-31 in two overtimes as No. 8 Texas Tech and No. 11 Tennessee fall
briefs.summary: Keyone Jenkins' 2-yard touchdown pass to Grayson Brousseau in the second overtime gave UCF its first win over a top-five team Saturday in Orlando, after BYU blocked a 47-yard field goal late in regulation; a top-two team has lost to an unranked opponent three weeks running. Cincinnati stunned Texas Tech 37-24 behind JC French IV's four touchdown passes, and Utah, 21-13 over No. 14 Houston, is the Big 12's only unbeaten at 7-0. In the SEC, No. 19 Texas blew a 21-point lead and still held on 34-27 against No. 7 Ole Miss, South Carolina took down Tennessee 27-24 on Malik Orsan's 48-yard field goal as time expired, and No. 13 Alabama handled Texas A&M 31-20. No. 6 Indiana won 13-6 in overtime at Michigan, its first win there since 1967; Wisconsin upset No. 16 USC 24-7, Minnesota took No. 15 Iowa 13-10 on a walk-off kick, and No. 1 Miami, atop the AP poll for the first time since 2002, rolled past Pitt 52-23.

briefs.headline: Rockets and 76ers alone at three wins as the Warriors and Heat open the NBA winless
briefs.summary: Joel Embiid posted a triple-double with LeBron James resting the first night of a back-to-back and Philadelphia ran its record to three wins without a loss, 127 to 116 over the Bucks on Saturday; Houston matched it in Atlanta with Kevin Durant scoring 22. Golden State lost its third straight, 131 to 122 in Phoenix as Devin Booker scored 43, a night after a 17 to 0 Memphis run erased a 12-point Warriors lead; Miami fell to Charlotte with Giannis Antetokounmpo fouling out again. Nikola Jokic's 199th triple-double, 35 points, 15 rebounds and 10 assists, and Jamal Murray's 42 carried Denver back from 23 down to an overtime win over New Orleans, and Jokic said booing home fans were not welcome. Cooper Flagg has a mild left shoulder sprain from a flagrant foul Friday in Indianapolis and sat out the Mavericks' home-opening loss Saturday; Orlando's Paolo Banchero is out multiple weeks with a high ankle sprain.

briefs.headline: Nylander hits 300 goals as the Maple Leafs rout the Oilers 7-2; Hellebuyck is a Devil
briefs.summary: William Nylander scored twice Saturday night in Edmonton, Anthony Stolarz made 30 saves and Toronto won its fourth straight; Leon Draisaitl scored both Oilers goals to tie Minnesota's Kirill Kaprizov for the league lead at 12, and Connor McDavid's two assists extended his season-opening points streak to 11 games and 33 points. On Friday the Devils acquired three-time Vezina Trophy winner Connor Hellebuyck from Winnipeg for Dawson Mercer, Nico Bjugstad, goaltender Nico Daws, another player and draft picks, ending a standoff that had kept the goaltender at home, and New Jersey won 3-1 over the Kings on Saturday for its third straight. Nikita Kucherov passed Steven Stamkos as the Lightning's career points leader with a first-period assist in Utah, where the Mammoth won in overtime.

briefs.headline: Aston Villa beat Manchester City 2-1 to end City's perfect start; Arsenal level on points
briefs.summary: Nicolas Jackson scored twice at Villa Park on Saturday to hand City its first Premier League defeat in eight matches; Arsenal's 2-0 over Everton, with goals from Ezri Konsa and Gabriel, left both on 21 points with City first on goal difference, plus 11 to plus 8. Brighton, a game in hand, is third on 16. Fulham won 1-0 at Coventry City to climb out of the bottom three, dropping Nottingham Forest, Coventry and Sunderland into the relegation places; Forest drew with Ipswich on Friday. Manchester United, 15th on seven points after seven matches, face Bournemouth on Sunday with Michael Carrick under pressure.

briefs.headline: Packers activate Jacobs for his 2026 debut as Kmet and Edmunds are lost for the season
briefs.summary: Green Bay activated running back Josh Jacobs on Saturday for Sunday's game against the Lions after six weeks on the commissioner's exempt list. The Eagles ruled out their top two receivers, DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks, for Monday night against the Cowboys, and the 49ers will be without Nick Bosa, Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel Sr. against the Falcons. Bears tight end Cole Kmet is out for the season with a right knee injury suffered in the win over New England, and Giants linebacker Tremaine Edmunds, the team's leading tackler and defensive signal-caller, is out for the year with a torn chest muscle. Minnesota activated Jordan Mason off injured reserve. Lawrence McCutcheon, the five-time Pro Bowl Rams running back, died Friday at 76.

briefs.headline: Sumo's autumn tour ends in Ube with both yokozuna through it, 14 days before Kyushu
briefs.summary: The 19-day autumn regional exhibition tour closed Sunday in Ube, Yamaguchi Prefecture, Daily Sports reported, with yokozuna (grand champion) Onosato, the September champion, saying he was glad to finish it without illness or withdrawal a year after a dislocated left shoulder cost him the final day in Fukuoka while tied for the lead. Hoshoryu, the other yokozuna, who has sat out three straight tournaments after right knee surgery in late July, joined the tour Oct. 10 and took practice bouts from its midpoint; his condition is improving gradually. The banzuke (rankings) for the Kyushu basho (tournament) is released Monday, and the tournament opens Nov. 8 at the Fukuoka Kokusai Center and runs to Nov. 22, per the Japan Sumo Association's year schedule, 14 days out, with tickets sold out.

waters.reading: 128 cfs, 1.78 feet at 5:15 a.m., falling on discharge and on stage against 174 cfs and 1.98 feet in the fetcher's comparison.
waters.working: Down 20 cfs and 0.09 feet on the day against the USGS trace's 148 cfs and 1.87 feet at 5:15 a.m. Saturday, and the river has crossed the line Thursday's desk was watching: it read 208 at 5:15 Thursday, eight above the fetcher's 200-cfs pushy threshold, 174 at 6 a.m. Friday, 148 Saturday and 128 this morning, an eighth straight falling morning with the recession still slowing (46, 34, 26, 20). The read string is the fetcher's own verdict, "128 cfs - prime wading water.", its band for 100 to 200 cfs, and the river sits 28 cfs above the floor of it. The fetcher's 174 cfs and 1.98 feet 24h_ago fields match the trace's first point at 6 a.m. Friday, about 47 hours old, so the 46-cfs drop they imply is two days' worth; the falling flags are right. At 128 and falling after a week of recession the Williams is the long-leader, small-fly problem the desk's instructions describe, not an edges problem: the pocket water, plunge pools and undercut banks the file records as its structure are wadeable across at this flow, the water is low and clear, and the fish in the pocket water and the plunge-pool tail-outs see the angler before the fly. Caddis, stoneflies and sculpin are the forage the file records, so a 12-foot leader to 6X with a size 16 to 18 caddis pupa or pheasant tail under a small yarn indicator or a dry-dropper off a size 14 to 16 elk-hair caddis, fished from downstream up the seams and the plunge-pool tail-outs in the afternoon; a size 8 to 10 weighted stonefly only in the deepest plunge pools; and the sculpin pattern, olive or black, swung under the undercut banks at first and last light, when the low clear water is least against it. The Williams River in Pocahontas and Webster counties is on WVDNR's fall trout stocking schedule, code F in the 2026 Fishing Regulations Summary as Thursday's desk read it, one stocking each week for two weeks beginning the third Monday of October, which was Oct. 19; the second week begins tomorrow, Monday, Oct. 26. WVDNR's fish-stocking page, which posts stockings by the end of each business day, listed no waters under 'The following waters were stocked' when opened at 5:51 this morning, a Sunday, so no delivery to the Williams, the Cranberry or the Summersville tailwater is confirmed. The fetcher carries no Williams water temperature, so none is printed.

waters.near: 14 miles above R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.reading: 24.43 feet at 5 a.m., falling against 24.87 in the fetcher's comparison.
waters.read: 24.4 ft and falling — normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: The fetcher reads the pool falling, down 0.44 against its 24.87 comparison point; against the USGS trace's 24.65 at 5 a.m. Saturday the gauge is down 0.22 on the day, inside the fetcher's 0.25-foot steady band, so the day alone would read steady and the falling flag is the comparison window's, though the direction is down. The trace shows the pool rose to 24.90 by 5 p.m. Saturday and came off 0.47 overnight to this morning's reading, which is the pool being worked, not a river rising. The read string is the fetcher's band verdict, normal pool, ordinary bank access, and at 24.4 the gauge is 2.6 feet under the up-and-pushing line at 27 feet; it read 24.99 Thursday. At normal pool the river fishes the structure and the current it makes, not the slack: shad are the forage and skipjack are with them, so a white or pearl swimbait on a half-ounce head or a three-quarter-ounce spoon worked down the current face of each wing dam and along the riprap where the current breaks; a half-ounce blade bait or a jigging spoon on the lock wall's deep edge for the sauger, which the cooling water and the full moon favor after dark; crawfish are the third forage the file records, so a crawfish-colored jig in the riprap for the smallmouth; and cut skipjack on the bottom in the barge cuts and the outside bends for the blues and flatheads after dark. What is above is still falling: the Williams at Dyer went 148 to 128 on the day. The Corps' Huntington District site was not opened and no lake elevation or release figure is printed.
waters.note: This is the gauge above R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam, the pool side; the Byrd tailwater is not gauged by USGS and is not printed. The fetcher's 24.87 comparison point is about 47 hours old, a hundredth off the 24.86 the P2D trace carries for 6 a.m. Friday, not 24 hours ago; against the trace's 24.65 at 5 a.m. Saturday the pool is down 0.22 on the day, inside the 0.25-foot steady band. The fetcher's number and flag are printed as the fetcher's and the comparison-window correction is here.

waters.read: 26.5 ft — normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: The fetcher reads the gauge steady, up 0.05 against its 26.42 comparison point, and that flag is wrong on the day: against the USGS trace's 26.16 at 5 a.m. Saturday the gauge is up 0.31, outside the fetcher's 0.25-foot steady band, and the trace shows it fell to 25.86 by 5 p.m. Saturday and came up 0.61 overnight while Point Pleasant above the dam came off 0.47 in the same hours, the signature of the dam passing water, though the Corps' Huntington District site was not opened and no release figure is printed. The read string is the fetcher's band verdict, normal pool, ordinary bank access, and at 26.5 the gauge is half a foot under the 27-foot line between that band and up and pushing, a seventh normal-pool morning; it read 26.37 Thursday. A pool coming up overnight below the dam puts current on the structure, which is where the fish hold: the forage is shad and skipjack with crawfish in the riprap, so a white swimbait or a three-quarter-ounce spoon worked down the current face of each wing dam rather than the eddy behind it; a half-ounce blade bait or a chartreuse-and-white paddletail on a half-ounce head along the riprap points in low light; a black-and-blue jig for the smallmouth and the drum in the rock; cut skipjack on the bottom in the barge cuts and the outside bends for the blues and the flatheads after dark; and the lock wall from the downstream side on a live skipjack for the hybrids while the gates are passing water.
waters.note: This is the gauge below R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam, not the tailwater. The fetcher's 26.42 comparison point is about 47 hours old, five hundredths off the 26.47 the P2D trace carries for 6 a.m. Friday, not 24 hours ago; against the trace's 26.16 at 5 a.m. Saturday the gauge is up 0.31 on the day, outside the 0.25-foot steady band, so the steady flag holds only against the window-start point and the day alone reads rising. The fetcher's number and flag are printed as the fetcher's and the comparison-window correction is here.

waters.reading: Sound at Hampstead: low 1:58 AM at 0.3 ft, high 8:05 AM at 4.4 ft, low 2:45 PM at 0.5 ft, high 8:24 PM at 3.8 ft. Surf at Ocean City Beach pier: low 12:38 AM at 0.1 ft, high 7:05 AM at 5.7 ft, low 1:24 PM at 0.1 ft, high 7:23 PM at 4.7 ft. Water 63.7F at Beaufort, 60 miles up the coast, observed 5:30 a.m. Moon full, 99% lit, 14.0 days old.
waters.read: Fish the moving water either side of high at 8:05 AM and 8:24 PM in the sound.
waters.working: Full moon and a gale: the fetcher's file carries the moon as full, 99 percent lit and 14.0 days old, the full falling at 04:12 UT Monday, Oct. 26, by the U.S. Naval Observatory table Wednesday's edition cited, not re-queried today, and the spring tides are here. The sound at Hampstead bottomed at 0.3 feet at 1:58 a.m., and is on its flood at press time, filling 4.1 feet to a 4.4-foot high at 8:05 a.m., the biggest swing since Thursday's edition; it drains 3.9 feet to a 0.5-foot low at 2:45 p.m., fills 3.3 feet to a 3.8-foot high at 8:24 p.m. and drains toward Monday's early low, which falls outside today's table. All four sound events land inside Sunday; nothing carries a spillover tag today. The surf at Ocean City Beach pier runs ahead and is the bigger water: low 12:38 a.m. at 0.1, high 7:05 a.m. at 5.7, low 1:24 p.m. at 0.1, high 7:23 p.m. at 4.7, a 5.6-foot flood against Thursday's 3.8. Today's lags from the two tables are 60 and 61 minutes on the highs and 80 and 81 minutes on the lows; the lows again lag longest, the shallow sound draining slower than it fills, which stretches the ebb at the crew's spot past what a flat offset would give. NWS Wilmington has the beach and the water covered this morning, the first Topsail products in four mornings: a Coastal Flood Advisory for Coastal Pender County until 9 p.m., up to one foot of inundation above ground level in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways, low-lying roads along the Intracoastal Waterway and adjacent tidal creeks named for minor flooding, which lands on the 8:05 a.m. and 8:24 p.m. sound highs; a Rip Current Statement for Coastal Pender, a High Rip Current Risk from 6 a.m. through 8 p.m. with a strong north-to-south longshore current; and a Gale Warning on the coastal waters from Surf City to Cape Fear out 20 nautical miles until 11 p.m., northeast winds 20 to 30 knots gusting 35 and seas up to 10 feet, strong winds the service says will cause hazardous seas that could capsize or damage vessels. The water at Beaufort, 60 miles up the coast, read 63.7 degrees at 5:30 a.m., down 1.4 from Thursday's edition reading of 65.1; the fetcher's file gives no reading at Topsail itself. What is running is the reference seasonal calendar, labeled as such and not a live report: the Fisherman's Post Topsail and Sneads Ferry October report, published Thursday, Oct. 1, at 9 a.m. ET, is 24 days old this morning and past the paper's 21-day gate, the feed still carried it as its newest item at 5:47 a.m., and no November report has posted. The calendar's October pattern is spot at the peak of the run, red drum, trout, bluefish, sea mullet and black drum; its November pattern, a week away, is red drum, speckled trout at their prime, bluefish, spot, sea mullet and blow toads, and the Beaufort thermometer dropping through 64 is the cool-down that pattern turns on. On today's tides and this water, a tide problem before it is a lure problem, and today the weather sets the water: the surf and the piers are under the Gale Warning and the High Rip Current Risk, with a northeast wind of 20 to 30 knots piling the ocean onto the beach, so the oceanfront is not the day's water and the sound inside the island is. The sound flood runs to 8:05 a.m. with 4.4 feet over the grass and up the dock pilings, the flooded-high stage where the drum push into the grass and the dock flats, finger mullet and shrimp the forage the file records, so a quarter-ounce gold spoon or a paddletail on a three-sixteenths-ounce head along the flooded grass edges and down the dock lines on the top of the flood, and a live shrimp on a slip cork at the oyster bars and the bridge pilings for the black drum and sheepshead as the bars go under. The ebb from 8:05 a.m. to 2:45 p.m. is the day's working window, 6 hours 40 minutes of falling water on a spring tide, harder current through the inlet and more bait pulled out of the marsh than on any day this month; the red drum stage, the last of the fall, is roughly 12:45 to 2:45 p.m., in full daylight, a live finger mullet on a Carolina rig or a three-inch Gulp shrimp under a popping cork fan-cast a couple of feet off the ICWW channel edge where the creek mouths drain the grass, a cut mullet chunk on the bottom at the same edge as the water gets low, and with a northeast wind on the water the lee shorelines and the creek mouths on the mainland side are where it can be cast. For spot, the calendar's October peak, a two-hook bottom rig with bloodworm or shrimp bits on the channel edges on the moving water either side of the 2:45 p.m. low. The flood from 2:45 to 8:24 p.m. covers the oyster bars and grass edges again, the same spoon and paddletail program, and dusk falls on the last of the flood, the trout window the calendar is a week from calling prime: a Spook Jr. or a suspending twitch bait walked over the deeper grass edges and the dock lights in the last hour of light, then a live shrimp under a slip cork in the deeper holes, 15 to 20 feet, on the first of the evening ebb after 8:24 p.m. Slack at 8:05 a.m., 2:45 p.m. and 8:24 p.m. is dead water, and on a spring tide the slack is short. Oysters are in their 11th day open under SF-1-2026 on the public bottom; the oyster bars the crew fishes over are the same structure, and the sanctuaries in rule 15A NCAC 03R .0117 are closed to harvest. Flounder are release only, the 41st day.
